sections.title: Mental model: how React updates the screen
sections.intro_md:
**Core idea:** `UI = f(state)`. You describe *what* the UI should look like for the current state; React figures out *how* to change the DOM.

```
   Trigger                 Render phase (pure, can be paused/redone)      Commit phase (sync)
 ┌─────────────┐         ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────────┐
 │ setState()  │         │ React calls your component functions    │     │ React applies the     │
 │ new props   │ ──────► │ → new element tree (virtual DOM)        │ ──► │ minimal DOM changes    │
 │ context     │         │ → diff with previous tree               │     │ → runs ref callbacks   │
 │ change      │         │   (reconciliation)                      │     │ → useLayoutEffect      │
 └─────────────┘         └────────────────────────────────────────┘     │ → browser paints       │
                                                                         │ → useEffect runs       │
                                                                         └──────────────────────┘
```

**Rules that follow from this:**
- Component functions must be **pure**: same props/state → same output, no side effects during render (React may call them more than once — Strict Mode does so deliberately in development).
- Side effects (network, subscriptions, timers) go in **event handlers** (user caused it) or **effects** (synchronising with an external system).
- A component re-renders when **its state changes, its parent re-renders, or a context it reads changes**.

**Where React fits in a typical AI app (your stack):**
```
 ┌──────────────────────────── Browser ────────────────────────────┐
 │  Vite-built React SPA                                            │
 │  ┌──────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  ┌───────────────────────────┐ │
 │  │ Router   │  │ Server-state   │  │ Chat UI                    │ │
 │  │ (URL =   │  │ cache (TanStack│  │ useAgentStream(sessionId)  │ │
 │  │ state)   │  │ Query)         │  │ → SSE/WebSocket tokens     │ │
 │  └──────────┘  └───────┬────────┘  └────────────┬──────────────┘ │
 └─────────────────────────┼────────────────────────┼────────────────┘
                           │ HTTPS + JWT (Cognito)   │ SSE stream
                           ▼                         ▼
                   FastAPI / API Gateway  ──►  Agent (LangGraph on AgentCore)
```

questions.title: What is React and what is a component?
questions.short_md: React is a JavaScript library for building UIs declaratively. A component is a function that takes **props** and returns **JSX** describing a piece of UI. Components compose into a tree.

questions.title: Props vs state vs derived values
questions.short_md:
- **Props**: inputs passed from the parent — read-only for the child.
- **State**: data the component *remembers* between renders; changing it triggers a re-render.
- **Derived values**: anything you can compute from props/state — **compute it during render, don't store it in state.**
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:**
- **Props**: inputs passed from the parent — read-only for the child.
- **State**: data the component *remembers* between renders; changing it triggers a re-render.
- **Derived values**: anything you can compute from props/state — **compute it during render, don't store it in state.**

**Example:**
```jsx
function DocList({ documents }) {
  const [filter, setFilter] = useState("all");                 // state
  const visible = documents.filter(d => filter === "all" || d.status === filter); // derived
  const doneCount = documents.filter(d => d.status === "done").length;            // derived
  // ❌ const [doneCount, setDoneCount] = useState(0) + an effect to sync it → can drift out of sync
  return <>{doneCount} done … {visible.map(d => <Row key={d.id} doc={d} />)}</>;
}
```

**Rule:** single source of truth. Duplicated state = bugs where two copies disagree.

questions.title: How does state update? Why is `setState` "async"?
questions.short_md: `setX(v)` doesn't change `x` immediately; it **schedules** a re-render. Inside the current render, `x` is a snapshot. React **batches** multiple updates (in all handlers since React 18) into one render.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** `setX(v)` doesn't change `x` immediately; it **schedules** a re-render. Inside the current render, `x` is a snapshot. React **batches** multiple updates (in all handlers since React 18) into one render.

**Example:**
```jsx
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
function handleClick() {
  setCount(count + 1);
  setCount(count + 1);       // both use the same snapshot (0) → result 1
  setCount(c => c + 1);      // updater function uses latest queued value → correct
  console.log(count);        // still 0 here – snapshot
}
```

**Immutable updates:** never mutate state objects; create new ones so React sees a new reference.
```jsx
setUser(u => ({ ...u, name: "Ana" }));                // ✅
setItems(items => [...items, newItem]);               // ✅
items.push(newItem); setItems(items);                 // ❌ same reference → may not re-render
```

questions.title: Why do list keys matter?
questions.short_md: Keys tell React **which item is which** between renders, so it can keep the right state and DOM for each row. Use a stable unique ID; avoid array index when the list can reorder, insert or delete.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** Keys tell React **which item is which** between renders, so it can keep the right state and DOM for each row. Use a stable unique ID; avoid array index when the list can reorder, insert or delete.

**Explanation:**
```
Before: [A(key=0), B(key=1)]   insert X at top → [X(key=0), A(key=1), B(key=2)]
With index keys React thinks "item 0 changed from A to X" → A's input text now shows on X's row ❌
With id keys   React sees "new X inserted, A and B unchanged" ✅
```

```jsx
{messages.map(m => <Message key={m.id} message={m} />)}
```

questions.title: Render vs commit
questions.short_md: **Render** = React calls your components to compute the new UI tree (pure, may be interrupted or repeated). **Commit** = React applies changes to the real DOM, then runs effects. Never do side effects in render.

questions.title: Controlled vs uncontrolled inputs
questions.short_md: **Controlled**: React state holds the value (`value` + `onChange`) — easy validation and syncing. **Uncontrolled**: the DOM holds the value; you read it via a `ref` or form data — less code, fewer re-renders.

questions.title: Lifting state up and prop drilling
questions.short_md: When two siblings need the same data, move the state to their **closest common parent** and pass it down as props. If you pass props through many layers that don't use them ("prop drilling"), consider **composition** (pass components as `children`) or **context**.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** When two siblings need the same data, move the state to their **closest common parent** and pass it down as props. If you pass props through many layers that don't use them ("prop drilling"), consider **composition** (pass components as `children`) or **context**.

```jsx
// Composition avoids drilling `user` through Layout
<Layout sidebar={<UserMenu user={user} />}>
  <Dashboard />
</Layout>
```

questions.title: Conditional rendering and fragments
questions.short_md: {isLoading && <Spinner />}                 // careful: {count && <X/>} renders "0" when count=0 {count > 0 ? <List /> : <Empty />} <>                                          {/* Fragment: group without an extra div */} <dt>Name</dt><dd>{name}</dd> </>
questions.body_md:
```jsx
{isLoading && <Spinner />}                 // careful: {count && <X/>} renders "0" when count=0
{count > 0 ? <List /> : <Empty />}
<>                                          {/* Fragment: group without an extra div */}
  <dt>Name</dt><dd>{name}</dd>
</>
```

questions.title: Class components vs function components
questions.short_md: Function components with Hooks are the modern standard. Class components (`this.state`, `componentDidMount`) still work and are still needed for **error boundaries** (no hook equivalent yet), but new code uses functions.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** Function components with Hooks are the modern standard. Class components (`this.state`, `componentDidMount`) still work and are still needed for **error boundaries** (no hook equivalent yet), but new code uses functions.

| Class lifecycle | Hook equivalent |
|---|---|
| `componentDidMount` / `componentDidUpdate` / `componentWillUnmount` | `useEffect(() => { …; return cleanup }, [deps])` |
| `shouldComponentUpdate` | `React.memo` |
| `this.state` | `useState` / `useReducer` |

questions.title: Rules of Hooks — and why they exist
questions.short_md: (1) Call hooks only at the **top level** of a component or custom hook — not inside loops, conditions or nested functions. (2) Call them only from React functions. Reason: React stores hook state in an ordered list per component and matches them **by call order** each render.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** (1) Call hooks only at the **top level** of a component or custom hook — not inside loops, conditions or nested functions. (2) Call them only from React functions. Reason: React stores hook state in an ordered list per component and matches them **by call order** each render.

```
Render 1: useState(A) → slot 0, useState(B) → slot 1, useEffect → slot 2
Render 2 with an `if` skipping first hook: useState(B) reads slot 0 → gets A's value ❌
```

```jsx
function Doc({ data }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);   // ✅ all hooks first
  if (!data) return null;                    // early return AFTER hooks
  …
}
```

(`use()` in React 19 is the one exception — it may be called conditionally.)

questions.title: `useState` vs `useReducer`
questions.short_md: `useState` for simple independent values. `useReducer` when the next state depends on the previous state through several **named transitions** — logic becomes a pure, testable function.

questions.title: What does `useEffect` actually do?
questions.short_md: It **synchronises your component with an external system** (WebSocket, browser API, third-party widget, non-React state) after the commit. It runs after paint, re-runs when dependencies change, and its **cleanup** runs before the next run and on unmount.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** It **synchronises your component with an external system** (WebSocket, browser API, third-party widget, non-React state) after the commit. It runs after paint, re-runs when dependencies change, and its **cleanup** runs before the next run and on unmount.

**Lifecycle:**
```
mount:        render → commit → paint → effect(sessionId=A)
deps change:  render → commit → paint → cleanup(A) → effect(sessionId=B)
unmount:      cleanup(B)
```

**Example:**
```jsx
useEffect(() => {
  const ws = new WebSocket(`wss://api/sessions/${sessionId}`);
  ws.onmessage = e => setMessages(m => [...m, JSON.parse(e.data)]);
  return () => ws.close();                 // cleanup prevents leaks & cross-session writes
}, [sessionId]);
```

**Dependency array:** `[]` → run once after mount; `[a, b]` → when a or b change; omitted → after every render.

**Strict Mode (dev only):** mounts → unmounts → remounts once to expose missing cleanup. If your effect breaks under this, it has a bug.

questions.title: When should you NOT use `useEffect`?
questions.short_md: Don't use effects for (1) values you can **compute during render**, (2) logic caused by a **user event** (put it in the handler), (3) resetting state when a prop changes (use a **key**), (4) data fetching where a library/framework can do it better.

questions.title: `useRef` — what is it for?
questions.short_md: A ref is a mutable box `{ current }` that **persists across renders without causing a re-render** when changed. Uses: DOM access (focus, scroll, measure) and storing non-visual values (timers, `AbortController`, previous value).

questions.title: `useMemo`, `useCallback`, `React.memo`
questions.short_md:
- `useMemo(fn, deps)` — cache a **computed value**.
- `useCallback(fn, deps)` — cache a **function identity**.
- `React.memo(Component)` — skip re-rendering a child if its props are shallow-equal.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:**
- `useMemo(fn, deps)` — cache a **computed value**.
- `useCallback(fn, deps)` — cache a **function identity**.
- `React.memo(Component)` — skip re-rendering a child if its props are shallow-equal.

They're **performance** tools only. `useCallback` alone does nothing useful unless the function is passed to a memoised child or used as an effect dependency.

```jsx
const filtered = useMemo(() => rows.filter(r => r.text.includes(q)), [rows, q]);
const onSelect = useCallback(id => setSelected(id), []);
const Row = React.memo(function Row({ row, onSelect }) { … });
```

**React Compiler (v1.0 stable since Oct 2025):** a build-time plugin that inserts this memoisation automatically. With it enabled, most manual `useMemo/useCallback` become unnecessary — but code must follow the Rules of React (purity, no mutation of props/state).

questions.title: `useContext` — when to use, when to avoid
questions.short_md: Context passes a value to any depth without props. Every consumer re-renders when the provider **value** changes. Good for low-frequency global values (theme, current user, locale, feature flags). Bad for high-frequency data (streaming tokens, mouse position) in one big provider.

questions.title: `useLayoutEffect`, `useId`, `useSyncExternalStore`, `useImperativeHandle`
questions.short_md:
| Hook | Use when |
|---|---|
| `useLayoutEffect` | measure DOM and update **before paint** (avoid flicker, e.g., tooltip position). Blocks paint — use sparingly |
| `useId` | stable unique IDs for accessibility (`htmlFor`/`aria-describedby`) that match on server & client |
| `useSyncExternalStore` | subscribe to an external store (browser API, custom store) safely with concurrent rendering |
| `useImperativeHandle` | expose a limited imperative API from a child (`ref.current.focus()`) |
questions.body_md:
| Hook | Use when |
|---|---|
| `useLayoutEffect` | measure DOM and update **before paint** (avoid flicker, e.g., tooltip position). Blocks paint — use sparingly |
| `useId` | stable unique IDs for accessibility (`htmlFor`/`aria-describedby`) that match on server & client |
| `useSyncExternalStore` | subscribe to an external store (browser API, custom store) safely with concurrent rendering |
| `useImperativeHandle` | expose a limited imperative API from a child (`ref.current.focus()`) |

questions.title: Stale closures
questions.short_md: Each render's functions "see" the props/state of **that** render. A timer, interval or subscription created in an earlier render keeps reading old values unless dependencies are correct or you use updater functions/refs.

questions.title: Custom hooks — design and testing
questions.short_md: A custom hook (`useSomething`) extracts reusable **stateful logic** (not UI). Each component calling it gets its own independent state.

questions.title: Concurrent rendering — what changed in React 18?
questions.short_md: React can **interrupt** a long render to handle an urgent update (typing), then resume. Enabled with `createRoot`. Also: **automatic batching** everywhere, `useTransition`, `useDeferredValue`, Suspense improvements, streaming SSR.
questions.body_md: **Short answer:** React can **interrupt** a long render to handle an urgent update (typing), then resume. Enabled with `createRoot`. Also: **automatic batching** everywhere, `useTransition`, `useDeferredValue`, Suspense improvements, streaming SSR.

questions.title: `useTransition` and `useDeferredValue`
questions.short_md:
Both mark work as **non-urgent** so urgent updates (keystrokes) stay responsive.
- `useTransition` — you control the **state update**: `startTransition(() => setFilter(v))`, with `isPending` for a spinner.
- `useDeferredValue` — you receive a **value** and want a lagging copy for expensive rendering.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** Both mark work as **non-urgent** so urgent updates (keystrokes) stay responsive.
- `useTransition` — you control the **state update**: `startTransition(() => setFilter(v))`, with `isPending` for a spinner.
- `useDeferredValue` — you receive a **value** and want a lagging copy for expensive rendering.

```jsx
const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
const deferredQuery = useDeferredValue(query);
<input value={query} onChange={e => setQuery(e.target.value)} />   // urgent: instant
<HugeList filter={deferredQuery} />                                 // can lag behind
```
**Pitfall:** these don't reduce **network** calls — still debounce API requests and paginate on the server.

questions.title: Suspense, `React.lazy` and code splitting
questions.short_md: `React.lazy(() => import("./X"))` loads a component's code on demand. `<Suspense fallback>` shows a placeholder while children are "suspended" (loading code or data via a Suspense-enabled source).
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** `React.lazy(() => import("./X"))` loads a component's code on demand. `<Suspense fallback>` shows a placeholder while children are "suspended" (loading code or data via a Suspense-enabled source).

```jsx
const PdfViewer = lazy(() => import("./PdfViewer"));     // separate chunk built by Vite
<Suspense fallback={<Spinner />}>
  {tab === "pdf" && <PdfViewer docId={id} />}
</Suspense>
```

questions.title: Error boundaries — what they catch and what they don't
questions.short_md: An error boundary catches errors thrown **during rendering, in lifecycle methods and constructors** of its descendants, and shows a fallback UI. It does **not** catch errors in event handlers, async code (`setTimeout`, promises), server errors, or errors in the boundary itself.

questions.title: React 19: Actions, `useActionState`, `useFormStatus`, `useOptimistic`
questions.short_md: An **Action** is an async function passed to a transition or `<form action>`. React manages pending state, errors and optimistic updates for you.

questions.title: The `use()` API and Server Components
questions.short_md:
- `use(promise)` reads a promise's value inside render (suspends until resolved); `use(Context)` reads context — and `use` can be called conditionally.
- **React Server Components (RSC)** run only on the server (in frameworks like Next.js), can access DB/secrets directly, send zero JS to the browser, and are composed with **Client Components** (`"use client"`). A plain Vite SPA doesn't use RSC by default.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:**
- `use(promise)` reads a promise's value inside render (suspends until resolved); `use(Context)` reads context — and `use` can be called conditionally.
- **React Server Components (RSC)** run only on the server (in frameworks like Next.js), can access DB/secrets directly, send zero JS to the browser, and are composed with **Client Components** (`"use client"`). A plain Vite SPA doesn't use RSC by default.

```
Server Component (fetches data, no JS shipped) ──► renders ──► Client Component ("use client", has state/handlers)
```

questions.title: React 19.2: `<Activity>` and other recent additions
questions.short_md: - **`<Activity mode="hidden">`** — hide part of the UI while **keeping its state** and deferring its updates (e.g., keep a chat tab's scroll and draft while another tab is shown; pre-render a likely next screen). - **`useEffectEvent`** — see Q18. - **Performance tracks** in Chrome DevTools showing React scheduler work. - Other React 19 niceties: `ref` as a prop, `<Context>` as provider, document metadata (`<title>`, `<meta>`) rendered anywhere and hoisted to `<head>`, better hydration error messages.
questions.body_md:
- **`<Activity mode="hidden">`** — hide part of the UI while **keeping its state** and deferring its updates (e.g., keep a chat tab's scroll and draft while another tab is shown; pre-render a likely next screen).
- **`useEffectEvent`** — see Q18.
- **Performance tracks** in Chrome DevTools showing React scheduler work.
- Other React 19 niceties: `ref` as a prop, `<Context>` as provider, document metadata (`<title>`, `<meta>`) rendered anywhere and hoisted to `<head>`, better hydration error messages.

questions.title: How do you organise state in a large app?
questions.short_md: Classify state by **who owns it**, then pick the tool:
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** Classify state by **who owns it**, then pick the tool:

| Kind of state | Example | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| Local UI | modal open, input draft | `useState` in the component |
| URL | selected doc, filters, page | router search params |
| **Server state** (cached copy of backend data) | document list, user profile | **TanStack Query / SWR / RTK Query** |
| Shared client state | sidebar layout, multi-step wizard | Zustand / Redux Toolkit / context |
| Form state | big forms | React Hook Form / form actions |

**Key insight:** most "global state" is really **server state** and needs caching, deduping, refetching and invalidation — not a hand-rolled Redux store.

questions.title: Server state with TanStack Query
questions.short_md: const { data, isPending, error } = useQuery({ queryKey: ["documents", tenantId, page],     // cache key — include everything that changes the result queryFn: ({ signal }) => api.listDocs(tenantId, page, { signal }),   // auto-abort staleTime: 30_000, });

questions.title: Race conditions in async fetching
questions.short_md: If the user switches from document A to B, A's slow response may arrive after B's and overwrite it. Fix: cancel superseded requests with `AbortController`, or ignore results whose request is no longer current (or use a query library keyed by ID).

questions.title: Optimistic updates
questions.short_md: Show the expected result immediately, send the request, then **confirm or roll back**. Needs a temporary ID and a reconciliation step.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** Show the expected result immediately, send the request, then **confirm or roll back**. Needs a temporary ID and a reconciliation step.

```
user sends message → add {id: "tmp-1", status: "pending"} → POST
   ├─ 201 {id: "m-42"} → replace tmp-1 with m-42, status "sent"
   └─ error           → mark tmp-1 "failed", show Retry
```

questions.title: Routing (React Router) basics
questions.short_md: - Routes map URL → component tree; nested routes share layouts (`<Outlet/>`). - Put shareable state (selected document, filters) in the URL so refresh/back button/deep links work. - Protect routes in the UI for UX, but **the server must still authorise** every request. - Lazy-load route components to split bundles.
questions.body_md:
- Routes map URL → component tree; nested routes share layouts (`<Outlet/>`).
- Put shareable state (selected document, filters) in the URL so refresh/back button/deep links work.
- Protect routes in the UI for UX, but **the server must still authorise** every request.
- Lazy-load route components to split bundles.

questions.title: Reconciliation and how component identity affects state
questions.short_md: React compares the new tree with the old by **position + type + key**. Same type at same position → keep state and update. Different type or key → unmount old (state lost), mount new.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** React compares the new tree with the old by **position + type + key**. Same type at same position → keep state and update. Different type or key → unmount old (state lost), mount new.

```jsx
<Editor key={documentId} doc={doc} />    // changing key = deliberately reset editor state
```

**Pitfall:** defining a component *inside* another component creates a new type every render → its state resets every time.
```jsx
function Parent() { const Child = () => <input/>; return <Child/>; }   // ❌ input loses focus each render
```

questions.title: How do you diagnose unnecessary re-renders?
questions.short_md: 1. **Measure** with React DevTools Profiler ("Highlight updates", flamegraph, "why did this render"). 2. Look for: a context whose value changes every render, new object/array/function props each render, state held too high in the tree, expensive work in render. 3. Fix: move state down / split components, memoise value or component, use selectors, virtualise long lists. 4. Re-measure. Don't optimise blindly.
questions.body_md:
1. **Measure** with React DevTools Profiler ("Highlight updates", flamegraph, "why did this render").
2. Look for: a context whose value changes every render, new object/array/function props each render, state held too high in the tree, expensive work in render.
3. Fix: move state down / split components, memoise value or component, use selectors, virtualise long lists.
4. Re-measure. Don't optimise blindly.

questions.title: Rendering long lists and streaming LLM text efficiently
questions.short_md:
- **Virtualise** long lists (only render visible rows) with `@tanstack/react-virtual` or `react-window`.
- For streaming tokens: append to **only the active message**, **batch** updates (e.g., flush every animation frame or ~50 ms), memoise completed messages so they don't re-render, render Markdown incrementally and safely.

questions.title: Bundle size and load performance
questions.short_md: - Code-split routes and heavy widgets (PDF viewer, charts) with `lazy`. - Tree-shake: import named functions (`import { debounce } from "lodash-es"`). - Analyse the bundle (`rollup-plugin-visualizer` with Vite). - Optimise images, preload critical fonts, measure **Core Web Vitals** (LCP, INP, CLS).
questions.body_md:
- Code-split routes and heavy widgets (PDF viewer, charts) with `lazy`.
- Tree-shake: import named functions (`import { debounce } from "lodash-es"`).
- Analyse the bundle (`rollup-plugin-visualizer` with Vite).
- Optimise images, preload critical fonts, measure **Core Web Vitals** (LCP, INP, CLS).

questions.title: Preventing XSS, especially with LLM output
questions.short_md: React escapes strings in JSX by default — `{text}` is safe. Danger comes from `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `javascript:` URLs in `href`, and Markdown/HTML renderers. Treat **all model output and retrieved documents as untrusted**.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** React escapes strings in JSX by default — `{text}` is safe. Danger comes from `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, `javascript:` URLs in `href`, and Markdown/HTML renderers. Treat **all model output and retrieved documents as untrusted**. ```jsx
{llmText}
// ✅ escaped
// ❌ unless sanitised import DOMPurify from "dompurify";
// sanitised {llmText} // react-markdown: no raw HTML by default ``` Also: validate link protocols (`http/https` only), set a **Content Security Policy**, and never put secrets in frontend code (everything in the bundle is public — including `VITE_*` env vars).

questions.title: Authentication vs authorisation in a React app
questions.short_md: **Authentication** = who you are (login, token). **Authorisation** = what you may do. The frontend uses auth state only for **UX** (hide buttons, redirect). The **server must enforce** authorisation on every request, because users can edit JS or call the API directly.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** **Authentication** = who you are (login, token). **Authorisation** = what you may do. The frontend uses auth state only for **UX** (hide buttons, redirect). The **server must enforce** authorisation on every request, because users can edit JS or call the API directly.

**Token storage:** HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies protect tokens from XSS-based theft (need CSRF protection); in-memory tokens + refresh flow are another option. Avoid long-lived tokens in `localStorage`.

questions.title: Testing React at multiple layers
questions.short_md: test("shows retry when upload fails", async () => { server.use(http.post("/api/upload", () => new HttpResponse(null, { status: 500 }))); render(<Uploader />); await userEvent.upload(screen.getByLabelText(/file/i), new File(["x"], "a.pdf")); expect(await screen.findByRole("button", { name: /retry/i })).toBeInTheDocument(); });

questions.title: Accessibility basics
questions.short_md: - Use semantic elements (`<button>`, `<nav>`, `<label htmlFor>`), not clickable `<div>`s. - Every input has a label; images have `alt`. - Keyboard navigation and visible focus; manage focus when opening modals. - Announce streaming/async updates with `aria-live="polite"` regions. - Check colour contrast; test with axe / Lighthouse.
questions.body_md:
- Use semantic elements (`<button>`, `<nav>`, `<label htmlFor>`), not clickable `<div>`s.
- Every input has a label; images have `alt`.
- Keyboard navigation and visible focus; manage focus when opening modals.
- Announce streaming/async updates with `aria-live="polite"` regions.
- Check colour contrast; test with axe / Lighthouse.

questions.title: Environment variables and config in a React SPA
questions.short_md: All config embedded in the bundle is **public**. Use build-time env vars only for non-secret values (API base URL, feature flags). Secrets (API keys) must stay on the server — the browser calls your backend, which calls the LLM.
questions.body_md: All config embedded in the bundle is **public**. Use build-time env vars only for non-secret values (API base URL, feature flags). Secrets (API keys) must stay on the server — the browser calls your backend, which calls the LLM.

questions.title: A chat view shows messages from the previous session after switching. What do you inspect?
questions.short_md: 1. **Effect cleanup** — is the old SSE/WebSocket aborted when `sessionId` changes? 2. **Cache keys** — does the query key include `sessionId` (and tenant/user)? 3. **Local state reset** — use `key={sessionId}` on the chat panel to reset drafts. 4. **Event routing** — tag stream events with session ID and drop mismatches. 5. **Backend** — verify the server authorises session ownership; if another *user's* data appears, it's a **security incident**, not a UI bug.
questions.body_md:
1. **Effect cleanup** — is the old SSE/WebSocket aborted when `sessionId` changes?
2. **Cache keys** — does the query key include `sessionId` (and tenant/user)?
3. **Local state reset** — use `key={sessionId}` on the chat panel to reset drafts.
4. **Event routing** — tag stream events with session ID and drop mismatches.
5. **Backend** — verify the server authorises session ownership; if another *user's* data appears, it's a **security incident**, not a UI bug.

questions.title: Design a UI for a long-running job (e.g., document extraction)
questions.short_md: states: queued → running(progress %) → partial → succeeded │                    └─► failed (retry) / cancelled ┌──────────── React ────────────┐        ┌──────── Backend ────────┐ │ POST /jobs → {jobId}           │ ─────► │ persists job in DB       │ │ subscribe SSE /jobs/{id}/events│ ◄───── │ emits progress events    │ │   (with Last-Event-ID resume)  │        │ with event ids           │ │ fallback: poll GET /jobs/{id}  │        │                          │ │ on reload: GET /jobs/{id}      │ ◄───── │ server is source of truth│ └────────────────────────────────┘        └──────────────────────…
questions.body_md:
```
 states: queued → running(progress %) → partial → succeeded
                       │                    └─► failed (retry) / cancelled
 ┌──────────── React ────────────┐        ┌──────── Backend ────────┐
 │ POST /jobs → {jobId}           │ ─────► │ persists job in DB       │
 │ subscribe SSE /jobs/{id}/events│ ◄───── │ emits progress events    │
 │   (with Last-Event-ID resume)  │        │ with event ids           │
 │ fallback: poll GET /jobs/{id}  │        │                          │
 │ on reload: GET /jobs/{id}      │ ◄───── │ server is source of truth│
 └────────────────────────────────┘        └──────────────────────────┘
```
Key points: explicit state machine, server-authoritative state, reconnect/resume, idempotent cancel, clear error and retry UX.

questions.title: A page re-renders the whole app on every streamed token. Fix?
questions.short_md: Profile → token state lives in a top-level context → every consumer re-renders. Move token state into the active message component or a store with selectors, batch token updates per animation frame, memoise finished messages, virtualise the transcript.
questions.body_md: Profile → token state lives in a top-level context → every consumer re-renders. Move token state into the active message component or a store with selectors, batch token updates per animation frame, memoise finished messages, virtualise the transcript.

questions.title: Users report the app is "frozen" while typing in a filter over 10k rows
questions.short_md: Rendering 10k rows on every keystroke blocks the main thread. Fixes in order: virtualise the list, `useDeferredValue` for the filter value, `useMemo` the filtering, move filtering to the server with debounced queries if data is larger.
questions.body_md: Rendering 10k rows on every keystroke blocks the main thread. Fixes in order: virtualise the list, `useDeferredValue` for the filter value, `useMemo` the filtering, move filtering to the server with debounced queries if data is larger.

questions.title: What do you check in a frontend PR before release?
questions.short_md: Correct state ownership (no duplicated state), effects have cleanup and correct deps, loading/empty/error states, request cancellation, XSS-safe rendering of model output, no secrets in bundle, accessibility, code splitting for heavy components, tests for main user flows and failure paths, monitoring (error reporting, web vitals).
questions.body_md: Correct state ownership (no duplicated state), effects have cleanup and correct deps, loading/empty/error states, request cancellation, XSS-safe rendering of model output, no secrets in bundle, accessibility, code splitting for heavy components, tests for main user flows and failure paths, monitoring (error reporting, web vitals).

questions.title: How do you type React components, state and events?
questions.short_md: Type **props** with a `type`/`interface`, let TypeScript **infer** most state, add generics only when inference can't (e.g. `null` initial value), and model UI states as **discriminated unions** so impossible states can't be represented.

sections.title: Cheat sheet
sections.intro_md:
| Concept | Remember |
|---|---|
| TS + React | type props; infer state; discriminated unions for UI states; `unknown` not `any` |
| UI = f(state) | describe, don't mutate DOM |
| Render vs commit | render pure; side effects in handlers/effects |
| `setState` | schedules re-render; snapshot; use updater `c => c + 1` |
| Immutability | new object/array for every update |
| Keys | stable IDs, not index |
| Hooks order | top level only, same order each render |
| `useEffect` | sync with external system; always clean up |
| Not an effect | derived values, event logic, reset via `key` |
| `useRef` | mutable, no re-render; DOM handles |
| Memo hooks | perf only; React Compiler can automate |
| Context | low-frequency values; split/memoise |
| Server state | TanStack Query, not hand-rolled global store |
| Races | `AbortController` / query keys |
| React 19 | Actions, `useActionState`, `useOptimistic`, `use`, ref-as-prop |
| React 19.2 | `<Activity>`, `useEffectEvent` |
| Error boundary | render errors only, not async/events |
| XSS | `{}` escapes; sanitise `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; LLM output untrusted |
| Security | UI hides; **server authorises** |
